# Atlassian ↔ AU Investor Standard Mapping — Autonomous Goal File

> **Source of truth:** [SOURCE-OF-TRUTH.md](./SOURCE-OF-TRUTH.md).
> **Sibling goal:** [reseller-module-goal.md](./reseller-module-goal.md).
> This file is the durable spec that drives the autonomous loop until every
> BlockID.au phase has (a) an Atlassian real-world reference milestone,
> (b) the AU-investor-standard artefacts expected there, and (c) a working
> next-step nudge engine that keeps a founder moving between them.

future `vestingStartDate` → 0 vested / all unvested; cliff-not-passed → 0 vested; past `vestingMonths` → 100% vested; mid-vesting linear post-cliff (24/48 = 50%); day-of-month regression to previous whole month (2028-01-14 vs start 2026-01-15 → 23 not 24 months — the subtle `-1` branch that silently under-vests founders one day per anniversary); 4dp rounding on both `vestedPct` and `unvestedPct` (13/48 * 25 = 6.7708 vested / 18.2292 unvested pinned bit-for-bit so a `Math.round(x*100)/100` regression to 2dp is caught); `null cliff_months` coerces to 0 (equity vests from month 0) — this branch also protects the "advisor with no cliff" case; (b) `mapTeamMember` row mapping — `email` / `role` / `is_active` null-safe defaults (`role='founder'` when missing, `is_active=true` when missing so a pre-migration row without the column doesn't disappear from the UI), string `equity_pct: "33.33"` coerced to `33.33` number (Supabase numeric → PostgREST string contract), unparseable `equity_pct: "not-a-number"` → `0` (safe default — never NaN into the cap-table total); (c) `getTeamMembers` — table `team_members`, filter shape `.eq("project_id",…)` + `.eq("is_active", true)` (soft-deleted rows never leak), `.order("equity_pct", {ascending:false})` (DESC so majority holders top the UI), returns `[]` on null-admin + supabase error + null data (three no-throw paths — plus a `console.error` on the error path with the exact `[blockid:equity] getTeamMembers failed` prefix pinned so grep-based ops runbooks stay accurate); (d) `addTeamMember` — 100% cap enforcement (existing 60% + new 50% → rejected with `"Total equity would exceed 100%"` + both figures formatted `%.2f` for the founder to see the arithmetic; NO insert happens on rejection so the cap-table remains clean), insert-error passthrough (`{ok:false, error: message}` — and critically NO `equity_events` "grant" side-effect on the insert-failure path so the audit log doesn't diverge from the actual DB state), happy path returns the mapped member + inserts a paired `equity_events` row with `event_type='grant'` + `equity_pct` + a description containing the grantee name AND role (so the /workspace/equity feed reads naturally), null-coercion of optional `email` / `vestingMonths` / `cliffMonths` / `vestingStartDate` when the caller omits them (never writes `undefined` — the `citext` + `int` + `date` columns each need explicit `null`); (e) `updateTeamMember` — 100% cap enforcement excludes the target member from the total (a founder editing self from 30% → 55% with another founder at 40% → allowed because 40+55=95 not 30+40+55=125), rejection formats both figures `%.2f` again, UPDATE-error passthrough, partial-update contract — ONLY the columns the caller passed are in the UPDATE payload (Object.keys sorted comparison pins this; `updated_at` is always added — a fresh ISO string per call), `equityPct` omission short-circuits the fetch-current + getTeamMembers round-trips entirely so an unrelated `{name: 'Renamed'}` edit costs one DB call not three; (f) `removeMember` — soft-delete (`is_active=false` + `updated_at` stamp — never a hard DELETE so the cap-table history survives), pairs with an `equity_events` `event_type='transfer'` row describing the returned pool (`"unallocated pool"` phrase pinned so the /workspace/equity feed's "returned to pool" copy stays in sync), UPDATE-error passthrough with NO event log on failure, `member fetch returns null` branch skips the event-log insert entirely (defensive against a deleted row race — the soft-delete UPDATE still runs so `ok:true` is honest); (g) `getEquitySummary` — aggregates `totalAllocated` across active members + computes `unallocated = 100 - totalAllocated` at 4dp (33.3333 * 2 = 66.6666 → 33.3334 unallocated pinned so a founder never sees `33.3333` vs `33.33340000000001` float noise), loads up to 50 `equity_events` ordered by `event_date DESC` for the /workspace/equity activity feed, mapEquityEvent snake_case `event_type` → camelCase `type`, null-admin degrades to `{members: [], events: [], totalAllocated: 0, unallocated: 100}` with zero DB calls, events-fetch error keeps members intact + returns `events: []` (partial-failure UX — never blank out the cap table because the audit feed hiccupped). Test harness: multi-table operations queue per-call `{data, error}` responses via `state.queue` (independent scripts for each table + terminal, no state leak across a single test's fetch → update → insert sequence), and per-call `state.calls[]` captures let `callsFor(table)` scope-check filter/payload assertions to the right chain. `vi.useFakeTimers()` + `vi.setSystemTime()` used in the calculateVesting cases; `vi.useRealTimers()` restored in `afterEach` so time-independent tests never inherit a frozen clock. All 36 green (`npx vitest run src/lib/equity.test.ts` → 36 passed / 360 ms); `npx tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.json` clean for the new file (only pre-existing unrelated valuation-module + scn-detect + digest-snapshot type drift already documented above remains). This closes the Phase-5 equity-surface test-coverage gap — every `web/src/lib` file the /workspace/equity + /workspace/esop tracker depends on now has colocated regression coverage under the test-gate. **shipped 2026-08-01 (P1-template-route-test):** colocated 20-case vitest for the previously-untested public GET `web/src/app/api/dataroom/template/route.ts` — the reference-material endpoint that serves the shipped `DATA_ROOM_STRUCTURE` `templateContent` bodies as `.md` attachments. Every founder-facing "download template" link on /guide/data-room and /dataroom/[folder] resolves through this route, so a silent regression here (e.g. dropping the `?name=` presence guard and returning a 500, dropping the `doc.type === "template"` filter and leaking upload-only placeholders like "Pitch Deck" as blank markdown, dropping the `[^a-zA-Z0-9\s-]` sanitiser and letting a template name with a `"` inject a broken Content-Disposition header) breaks the P1_dataroom_map exit criterion's "every 'missing' template flagged P0 has a follow-up task" promise for the shipped-body half of the taxonomy. Pins: (a) `dynamic = "force-dynamic"` export — templates evolve out-of-band with app builds (marketing updates without a redeploy), so a Next prerender would ship stale bodies; (b) `?name=` presence guard — `null` (no param) AND `""` (present but empty via `?name=`) both 400 with `error` containing `/name/i` so a switch to `if (name === null)` doesn't 200-and-loop through the entire taxonomy on an empty lookup; (c) exact-name lookup contract — case-sensitive (`executive summary` → 404 even though `Executive Summary` exists), no trim (trailing whitespace 404s), unknown name → 404 with the queried name echoed in the error body; (d) `type` filter contract — `upload` (Pitch Deck), `connect` (Register of Members (Share Register)) 404 even when the name matches, AND the three rows that ship a `templateContent` but are typed `connect`/`auto` (Cap Table (Current + Post-raise) / Traction Dashboard / Due Diligence Checklist (Auto-generated)) each 404 so the connect/auto-populated flows can't be bypassed by a curl-and-download hack; (f) filename sanitisation — `[^a-zA-Z0-9\s-]` stripped then `\s+` collapsed to `-`, then `-template.md` appended: `Executive Summary` → `Executive-Summary-template.md`, `Market Size Analysis (TAM/SAM/SOM)` → `Market-Size-Analysis-TAMSAMSOM-template.md` (parens + slashes stripped, spaces collapsed), `Go-to-Market Strategy` → `Go-to-Market-Strategy-template.md` (source-side hyphens survive the whitelist), `Customer / User List` → `Customer-User-List-template.md` (the `\s+` `+` quantifier collapses the double-space left by removing `/`); ""` fallback → regex fails; (e) reserved-ticker guard fires for every one of the 7 shipped tickers with a helpful error message that contains `"<TICKER>"` + the word `reserved` + the `ticker_hint` field marker; guard is case-insensitive via the uppercase normaliser so a founder submitting "  btc  " still hits the `"BTC"` reserved branch; guard short-circuits BEFORE any supabase round-trip so a reserved ticker never triggers a rate-limit-consuming DB probe; (f) `getSupabaseAdmin() === null` → `{ok:false, error:"Service unavailable"}` with no DB access (the graceful-degrade path when the Supabase env is misconfigured); (g) insert branch (no existing row) — targets `startup_package_reserved_allocations`, INSERT payload shape pinned to `{project_id, pct_reserved, ticker_hint, created_at, updated_at}` with created_at + updated_at both stamped as parseable ISO strings AND identical (proves the same `now` is used for both on insert — a founder never sees a created_at LATER than updated_at, which would flip the "recently updated" sort direction in the admin dashboard); First test coverage for `email-enhanced.ts` — the AFSL-disclaimer-locale contract, the opt-out short-circuit (`svi_alerts` category), and the pdf/docx attachment MIME/filename pair are now regression-guarded so a founder-facing SVI-report email can't silently ship English disclaimers to a vi founder, spam an unsubscribed founder, or drop the downloadable pack attachment slot.
    depends_on: [P3_nudge_engine_impl, P5_investor_readiness_score]
    exit_criteria:
      - digest section "Your investor readiness this week" renders {score band, delta vs last week, single next action, top-3 missing}  # follow-up P7a — this cron ships the investor persona (Bloomberg-style watchlist recap); the founder persona (readiness recap) is next
      - opt-out honoured via existing email_preferences.weekly_digest flag (web/src/lib/email-preferences.ts:232)  # done (canSendEmail(email, "weekly_reports"); actual EmailCategory in current schema is weekly_reports, weekly_digest is a stale name)
      - dry-run harness prints a sample digest for admin@blockid.au  # done (`?skip_email=1` returns dry_run[] with per-investor subject + ticker_count)

    status: human_blocked

  P9_ship:
    status: done
    depends_on: [P3, P4, P5, P6, P7, P8]
    description: Ship-readiness — regression tests for legal + walkthrough + ship surfaces, CHANGELOG entry, and E2E walkthrough sign-off. **shipped 2026-08-08 (P9-onboarding-sequence-route-test):** colocated 26-case vitest for `web/src/app/api/cron/onboarding-sequence/route.ts` — the pre-analysis mailer that fires the 3-touch onboarding sequence (D+1 workspace-ready welcome, D+3 Evidence Vault CTA, D+7 Founding 100 A$5 scarcity pitch) to users who have signed up but NOT yet run an SVI analysis; the /api/cron/email-drip + /api/cron/weekly-insights mailers take over once a report is produced. Silent regressions the suite pins: (a) loss of `export const dynamic = "force-dynamic"` (a static build would freeze the sent:0/skipped:0 envelope and neither the sendEmail call nor the svi_notifications insert would ever fire); (b) loss of `export const maxDuration = 60` (crontab wrapper would kill mid-batch on D+3 users with many prior notifications); (c) loss of the CRON_SECRET bearer gate (unauth requests would leak the pre-analysis user list AND actually send email) — includes case-sensitivity check on `bearer` (lowercase must fail); (d) loss of the getSupabaseAdmin() null-guard (mis-configured env would throw at the first `.from(...)` instead of returning the 503 `ok:false` envelope); (e) breakage of the MAX_BATCH=20 cap that protects the mail transport when a signup backfill lands (25-user fixture proves only 20 fire); (f) drift on the step selection windows — D+1 fires in [1..4], D+3 in [3..6], D+7 in [7..10] (a user 11 days in must get nothing, a user 0 days in must get nothing); (g) breakage of the notification-dedupe SELECT — a pre-existing `svi_notifications` row with matching (email, notification_type) MUST cause the step to be skipped, or D+1 would re-send every tick until the user churned; (h) breakage of the one-email-per-user-per-run rule — after a successful send the inner loop MUST `break` so a fresh 1-day-old user does not immediately receive D+3 on the same tick; (i) branching on canSendEmail — a false verdict MUST increment `skipped` and NOT call sendEmail and NOT insert an svi_notifications row (dedupe would otherwise silently swallow the D+1 forever); pinned by asserting `canSendEmail(email, "weekly_reports")` is the exact call shape; (j) the notification row natural key `{email, account_id:null, notification_type}` (dedupe SELECT relies on it and the downstream lifecycle handoff keys on account_id:null to distinguish pre-analysis rows); (k) firstName derivation — `display_name?.split(" ")[0] ?? "there"` prevents `null,` subject drift on users who never set a display_name and trims a "Ada Lovelace" full name to "Ada"; (l) null-safe row hygiene — rows with null `email` or null `created_at` are skipped without throwing and without incrementing either counter (the users table has been observed with nulls in both columns); (m) envelope contract `{ok, sent, skipped, policy: "onboarding_3_emails_pre_analysis"}` — the crontab log aggregator keys on the policy tag and drift here loses the pre-analysis metric on the daily digest; (n) the 500 error envelope `{ok:false, error}` when the users query throws (crontab wrapper counts the 500 as a hard failure and retries; a missing `ok:false` would be classified as a soft success); (o) POST↔GET parity — the route uses `export { GET as POST }` so the crontab may hit either verb; the test pins `POST === GET` at the module level, and (p) the per-step subject strings and notification_type values are pinned to their D+1 / D+3 / D+7 exact-match forms so re-branding a subject line does not silently deduplicate wrong. Ships a small in-memory fake `SupabaseClient` covering the three query shapes the route uses — `.from("users").select().not().order().limit()` returning the pre-analysis user list, `.from("svi_notifications").select("id", {count:"exact", head:true}).eq("email",…).eq("notification_type",…)` returning `{count}` for the dedupe SELECT, and `.from("svi_notifications").insert(…)` recording the natural-key row — with per-branch failure injection via `state.throwOnUsersQuery`. Mocks `@/lib/email` (sendEmail only), `@/lib/email-preferences` (canSendEmail + ensureEmailPreferences + getUnsubscribeUrl + getPreferencesUrl stubbed to sentinel URLs so the wiring is pinned without depending on builder internals), and `@/lib/supabase` (getSupabaseAdmin swappable to null for the 503 case). All 26 cases pass under `vitest run` in ~400ms (transform 108ms, import 187ms, tests 57ms), colocated per web/AGENTS.md so the test-gate reverts the route change if the natural key or the step-selection window regresses. Prior sub-ship (2026-08-08, P9-email-drip-route-test): colocated 24-case vitest for `web/src/app/api/cron/email-drip/route.ts` — the only mailer that fires the 5-touch CCSO onboarding sequence (D1/D3/D7/D14 tips + D30 NPS) after a founder's first SVI report. Silent regressions the suite pins against: (a) losing `export const dynamic = "force-dynamic"` so the two DB writes (markSent / markFailed) stop firing under a static build; (b) losing the CRON_SECRET bearer gate so unauth requests leak queue depth and actually send email; (c) breaking POST↔GET parity so the server crontab (POST retryable / GET health-check) diverges; (d) regressing the BATCH_LIMIT=50 cap that protects the transport from queue-of-doom incidents when a backfill lands a huge batch; (e) branch drift on the send outcome — `ok:true` MUST call markSent (never markFailed) and count toward `sent`; `ok:false` MUST call markFailed with `send failed: <reason>` and count toward `failed`; a thrown exception MUST also call markFailed with the caught message (drips never re-queue silently); (f) the `failures[]` envelope truncation to 5 (unbounded failures balloon the JSONL log and OOM the crontab wrapper); (g) the unsubscribe URL formatting — every send MUST carry an `/unsubscribe?email=<url-encoded>` link keyed on the recipient (Spam Act 2003 (Cth) compliance) with the site origin normalised (trailing-slash stripped, defaulted to https://blockid.au when NEXT_PUBLIC_SITE_URL is unset); (h) skipping renderDripBody's per-drip campaign routing so every recipient receives the same body regardless of campaign (e.g. a D14 pricing pitch to a D1 recipient). Mocks `@/lib/email` (sendEmail only) and `@/lib/email-drip` (dueDrips, markSent, markFailed, renderDripBody) with per-branch vi.fn control; the renderer stub returns a per-campaign tagged subject/html/text so tests can prove the route routes the campaign string through untouched. Cases: (1) route-module shape — dynamic="force-dynamic" pinned, maxDuration=60 pinned; (2) auth gate — 401 without header, 401 with wrong bearer, 401 when CRON_SECRET unset, 401 when CRON_SECRET empty with bare `Bearer ` header, 401 when 'bearer' lowercased; (3) empty-queue path — 200 envelope {ok:true, considered:0, sent:0, failed:0, cap:50, failures:[]} with zero sendEmail / markSent / markFailed calls, dueDrips invoked as (Date, 50); (4) happy path — sendEmail ok:true triggers markSent(id) (never markFailed) with sent counter incremented, per-drip campaign strings routed through renderDripBody untouched (onboarding_d1 / onboarding_d14 / nps_d30 mixed batch preserves order and forwards email+payload verbatim), unsubscribe URL is `/unsubscribe?email=<url-encoded>` keyed on the recipient including `+`-tagged addresses, trailing-slash on NEXT_PUBLIC_SITE_URL is stripped before build, default origin is https://blockid.au when the env var is missing, null payload is normalised to `{}` before rendering; (5) failure branches — ok:false persists `send failed: <reason>` via markFailed and records `<campaign>:<reason>` in failures[], thrown Error persists err.message, non-Error throws are String()-coerced (raw string preserved), a single failure does NOT abort the batch (2 subsequent sends still complete and mark sent), 8-failure batch caps failures[] at exactly 5 entries with counters unaffected; (6) envelope contract — exactly {ok, considered, sent, failed, cap, failures} keys (no drift), Content-Type application/json; (7) GET parity — GET 401s without auth (same handle()), GET 200 envelope keys and cap:50 identical to POST. **shipped 2026-08-08 (P9-track-open-route-test):** colocated 20-case vitest for `web/src/app/api/track/open/route.ts` — the public 1x1 GIF tracking pixel embedded in every SVI report email (fetched by ~every mail client on the internet, from IPs we do not control). Silent regressions this suite pins against: (a) losing `export const dynamic = "force-dynamic"` so the pixel becomes a static export and the two DB writes never fire in production; (b) regressing the response body away from a valid 1x1 GIF (magic bytes GIF87a/GIF89a, sub-100-byte size, deterministic across requests) — every mail client would render a broken-image icon in the founder's report; (c) regressing Content-Type: image/gif; (d) regressing the anti-cache headers (Cache-Control no-store, no-cache, must-revalidate, max-age=0 + Pragma no-cache) — a cached pixel means the second, third, Nth open silently stop counting; (e) skipping the (slug, email) guard so a bare /api/track/open request touches supabase with undefined filters and fans an UPDATE across the whole table; (f) regressing the pinned table names or filters — `svi_notifications` filtered by (notification_type='svi_report', opened_at IS NULL) and `svi_analyses` filtered by (id=slug, viewed_at IS NULL) — losing the IS NULL guards would clobber first-opened-at with last-opened-at, turning open-count analytics into last-touched analytics; (g) not terminally `.then()`-awaiting the fire-and-forget builder chain so the write never dispatches; (h) failing to serve the 200 pixel on a null supabase client — mail clients would see a broken image icon in an unconfigured env. Mocks `@/lib/supabase` (`getSupabaseAdmin` only) with a chainable fake exposing `from → update → eq → is → then` and per-table capture of payload / eq / is filters + terminal-then flag. Cases: dynamic-export force-dynamic pin (1); pixel body — HTTP 200 on a bare GET, image/gif Content-Type, GIF magic-header bytes, sub-100-byte deterministic body identical across requests (5); anti-cache headers — Cache-Control + Pragma (2); query-param guard — no getSupabaseAdmin call when slug missing / email missing / both missing, pixel still served on partial params (4); happy path — one getSupabaseAdmin call, svi_notifications update payload + eq + is filters, svi_analyses update payload + eq (id=slug) + is filters, both updates issued, both terminally .then()-awaited, 200 GIF still served after DB writes (6); graceful degradation — 200 GIF on null supabase, still valid GIF bytes (2). All 20 green (`npx vitest run src/app/api/track/open/route.test.ts` → 20 passed / 385ms). Prior shipping note (superseded, kept in git history): **shipped 2026-08-08 (P9-admin-goal-loop-status-route-test):** colocated 15-case vitest for the previously-untested `web/src/app/api/admin/goal-loop-status/route.ts` — the read-only admin endpoint that merges the three `/tmp/blockid-*-loop.status` snapshots (reseller / atlassian / ux_ia) written every tick by `scripts/cron/goal-loop.mjs` into a single `{ ok, loops: {reseller, atlassian, ux_ia}, generated_at }` envelope for the admin dashboards. Silent regressions this suite pins against: (a) dropping the requireAdmin() gate so any authenticated user sees internal loop state; (b) dropping the getCurrentUser() null-user guard so a stranger sees internal loop state; (c) renaming any of the three fixed `/tmp/blockid-*-loop.status` paths so the panel silently returns null forever; (d) drifting the fixed three-key `{reseller, atlassian, ux_ia}` shape the admin dashboards key off; (e) losing the "unreadable / unparseable file → null" soft-fail so a never-fired loop 500s the admin dashboard instead of surfacing `null`; (f) losing `export const dynamic = "force-dynamic"` so the per-request auth read gets pinned to a build-time cache. Mocks `@/lib/auth` (partial — `getCurrentUser` only, preserves the real `ADMIN_EMAIL` constant so the real `requireAdmin()` from `@/lib/reseller/require-admin` runs unmocked and the email + role admin-path both stay under test) and `node:fs/promises` (per-path `readFile` fake defaulting to ENOENT on every path so the "never fired" state is the baseline; individual cases override to return valid JSON, torn-write / unparseable JSON, or a mix). Cases: dynamic-export force-dynamic pin (1); auth gate — 401 `no_user` on null user, 401 `not_admin` on authenticated non-admin, no disk I/O on unauthenticated / non-admin callers (state leak guard), role='admin' promotes a non-primary-email caller to admin (5); file-read wiring — exactly the three documented `/tmp/blockid-{reseller,atlassian,ux_ia}-loop.status` paths are read (rename regression guard), every read requests `utf8` encoding (Buffer would break JSON.parse) (2); payload shape — happy-path returns `{ok: true, loops, generated_at}`, exposes exactly the three keys `{atlassian, reseller, ux_ia}` on the loops envelope, `generated_at` parses as ISO-8601 via `Date.parse` (3); soft-fail — every ENOENT maps to `null` (never-fired loops surface as null not 500), JSON.parse failures on a torn write map to `null`, a parsed JSON snapshot threads through unchanged when the file is readable, mixed readable + missing files stay independent (one unreadable file does not blank the others) (4). (6) **fresh-mock discipline** — every test resets `issuerKeyConfiguredMock` + `publicJwkMock` in `beforeEach` and vi.restoreAllMocks in `afterEach` so state can't leak between the 503 / 200 / branch-selection describes. The suite pins seven contract surfaces: (1) **module surface** — `dynamic = "force-dynamic"` so the pack is never statically cached (a static cache on a mutable pack row would freeze `viewCount` and stale-serve a pre-update snapshot); (8) **caller-verbatim status + notes** — no server-side coercion (`in_progress` passes through unchanged; empty-string notes pass through — admins may deliberately clear a note). (9) **method isolation** — GET never calls `.update()`; POST never calls `.select()/.order()/.limit()` (proves the two branches are cleanly separated and a future refactor can't accidentally fuse them). (10) **`dynamic = "force-dynamic"`** — the route reads per-request auth state and must NOT be pinned to a build-time cache. (b) invalid_filename guard — `""` (empty), `"../etc/passwd.md"` (path traversal), `"nested/report.md"` (forward-slash), `"nested\\report.md"` (backslash), `"_daily-report-template.md"` (underscore-prefixed internal scaffold), `"report.txt"` (non-markdown extension), `"report"` (bare extensionless) all return 400 `{ok:false, reason:"invalid_filename"}` AND critically never touch fs — the mock reads array is empty on every rejection so a traversal probe cannot even trigger a filesystem lookup that a symlink attack could exploit; (c) not_found path — when neither candidate exists, 404 `{ok:false, reason:"not_found"}` is returned AFTER both `repo-root` and `web-workspace` candidates are tried in order (mock reads array matches `[web/content/reports, content/reports]` exactly — a silent skip of the second candidate would 404 the entire route under one of the two supported Next.js startup layouts); (d) dual-cwd candidate lookup — when the repo-root candidate exists, the web-workspace candidate is NOT tried (short-circuit pinned on `reads.length === 1`); when the repo-root candidate is missing but the web-workspace one exists, both are tried in order and the body from the web-workspace candidate is served — critical for local `cd web && npm run dev` vs `cd blockid.au && node web/.next/standalone/server.js` layouts; (e) hardening headers — `content-type: text/markdown; charset=utf-8` (blocks MIME sniff to HTML), `content-disposition: attachment; filename="..."` starts with `attachment;` (blocks inline preview), contains `filename="` prefix and `.md"` suffix (blocks header-injection via unclosed quotes), `x-content-type-options: nosniff` (belt-and-braces against browsers that override the content-type on sniff), `referrer-policy: no-referrer` (blocks downstream sites from back-tracing the download in referrer logs), `cache-control` contains `public` + `max-age=3600` + `s-maxage=3600` (CDN can absorb the fan-out — a drop would hammer the origin route on every download); (e) `log_tail` capped at 4000 chars + `stderr_tail` at 2000 chars — with a 9000-char stdout fixture the response body stays bounded AND the trailing smoke line survives (tail-slice not head-slice); (f) manifest read robustness — the fixed `/home/dovanlong/blockid.au/web/.deploy-manifest.json` path is read twice per request (pre + post sha diff), `git_sha` field is preferred but `sha` fallback covers older manifest formats, a rejecting `readFile` (ENOENT on a fresh box / first deploy) surfaces `pre_sha=null` + `post_sha=null` in the `deploy_incidents.detail` payload without throwing, and `rolled_back_to` falls back to the caller-supplied `target_sha` when the manifest is unreadable; (g) resolved-state stamping — `resolved_at` (ISO string) + `resolved_by` (admin email) are set only when `exit_code=0 AND smoke_passed=true`, both stay `null` when the rollback exits 0 but fails smoke (partial-success case that must NOT auto-resolve the incident); (h) smoke-inference regex — `✗ smoke` line flips false, `smoke fail` substring flips false, `smoke ok` / `smoke ✓` flips true, no-smoke-assertion-at-all defaults to false (defensive posture — an unproven rollback is not a passed rollback); (i) Telegram summary — the outbound line names the admin + `rolled_back_to` sha + `smoke ok`/`smoke FAIL` verdict, and a rejecting `sendTelegram` is swallowed so a Telegram outage cannot swallow the HTTP 200 response; (j) body-parsing tolerance — a bodyless POST + a malformed-JSON body both fall through to the default rollback without throwing (an admin double-clicking the button shouldn't 500), and the `application/x-www-form-urlencoded` fallback path forwards `target_sha` + `reason` into the spawn argv + `deploy_incidents.detail` respectively. Ships a synthetic `spawn()` double built on `EventEmitter` (stdout + stderr streams emit `data` Buffers synchronously; `close` fires on next tick with the requested exit code; `error` path emits on a delay before `close` to model missing-bash / missing-script) so the route's Promise-around-child-process contract is asserted end-to-end without touching a real shell. All 35 green (`npx vitest run src/app/api/admin/rollback/route.test.ts` → 35 passed / 434 ms); `npx tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.json` clean for the new file (only the pre-existing unrelated valuation-module drift already documented above remains). First test coverage for `api/admin/rollback/route.ts` — the deploy-script shell-out contract (admin-only, hex-sha-only, incident-audited, smoke-inferred, telegram-notified) is now regression-pinned so the one-click rollback button cannot silently drift into a footgun during future refactors. **shipped 2026-08-08 (P9-pitch-deck-route-test):** colocated 14-case vitest for the previously-untested `web/src/app/api/pitch-deck/route.ts` — the public GET that renders and streams the 12-slide BlockID Antler pitch deck PDF handed out on Twitter/LinkedIn/cold intros. Silent regressions pinned: (a) dropping the `enforceRateLimit("pitch-deck-public", null, request, 20, 60*60*1000)` guard so a public flood of GETs stalls the single-instance Node event loop on synchronous `@react-pdf` `renderToBuffer` CPU work (the guard IS the reason the route survives being public — pinned exact route-key + null-identity + max=20 + 1h window + request-pass-through so the limiter can read `cf-connecting-ip` instead of collapsing every caller to `"anon"`); (b) losing the early return on the limiter's 429 so the render still runs when the limiter says no (also verifies `PitchDeckPDF()` + `renderToBuffer` are never called on the rate-limited branch and the limiter's `Retry-After` header is passed through verbatim); (c) regressing `Content-Type` from `application/pdf` (browsers would download-as-octet-stream instead of preview-inline); (d) drifting `Content-Disposition` — the exact `inline; filename="BlockID-Pitch-Deck-Antler-2026.pdf"` is what we hand out, flipping `inline`→`attachment` forces every visitor into a download and renaming the filename rots every existing hotlink in shared decks/DMs; (e) losing `Cache-Control: public, max-age=3600` so every hit re-renders the PDF (CPU cost) and switching to `private`/`no-store` defeats the CDN/browser reuse we deliberately allow because this deck is public; (f) leaking the underlying `@react-pdf` error message / stack in the 500 body — the route deliberately returns a fixed `{ error: "Failed to generate pitch deck" }` string, not `err.message`, so a library version / filesystem path cannot leak to an anonymous caller; (g) losing the 500 `Content-Type: application/json` so the caller banner cannot parse the error envelope; (h) losing `export const dynamic = "force-dynamic"` so the per-request rate-limit read is pinned to a build-time snapshot and every visitor gets the same cached response with the limiter silently disabled at build time; (i) invoking `PitchDeckPDF()` more than once per request (doubles the CPU cost per hit); (j) reversing the limiter → factory → renderer call order so the expensive synchronous PDF work runs BEFORE the rate check has a chance to short-circuit; (k) losing the `console.error` breadcrumb on the catch branch — the admin log tail is the only signal we have that the public URL is broken (no external alerting on this route). Mocks `@/lib/rate-limit` (`enforceRateLimit` → `null` by default; per-test overridden to return a fake 429), `@react-pdf/renderer` (`renderToBuffer` → fake `%PDF-1.7` buffer), and `@/lib/pdf/pitch-deck-pdf` (`PitchDeckPDF` → sentinel element) so the tests exercise the route contract without spinning up react-pdf or hitting the real rate-limit store. Runtime: 14 passed / 349 ms. **shipped 2026-08-08 (P9-prune-rate-limits-route-test):** colocated 24-case vitest for `web/src/app/api/cron/prune-rate-limits/route.ts` — the CRON-secret-gated cleanup endpoint that calls the `prune_rate_limits(older_than)` SQL helper (migration 0107_rate_limits.sql) to evict expired rows from the persistent rate-limit table so it doesn't grow unbounded. Silent regressions this suite pins against: (a) losing `if (!secret) return false` in `authorised()` so a deploy with an unset `CRON_SECRET` env accepts anonymous callers and lets any visitor pound the SQL RPC; (b) accepting a case-insensitive `bearer <secret>` prefix, opening the door to header-normalisation quirks in reverse proxies; (c) accepting the bare secret without the `Bearer ` prefix; (d) losing the `getSupabaseAdmin() === null` 503 branch so a mis-configured Supabase env 500s the whole tick instead of the graceful `{ok:false, error:"supabase_unavailable"}` envelope; (e) widening the `/^[0-9]+\s+(minute|minutes|hour|hours|day|days)$/i` interval whitelist regex — the exact class of bug that lets `?interval=1 hour; DROP TABLE rate_limits` reach `supabase.rpc()` as an arbitrary string, since the older_than parameter is spliced directly into a Postgres INTERVAL cast in the SQL helper; (f) dropping the case-insensitive `i` flag or the `\s+` inter-token whitespace requirement so a valid `?interval=6%20hours` request silently falls back to the 2-hour default and prunes too aggressively; (g) changing the default fallback away from `"2 hours"` — the retention window every crontab entry assumes; (h) renaming the `prune_rate_limits` RPC or the `older_than` param name so the RPC round-trip 404s at runtime; (i) losing the `typeof data === "number"` coercion so a null/string RPC reply crashes the JSON serialiser instead of degrading to `pruned: 0`; (j) losing the interval echo in the 500 error envelope so ops can't tell which window failed; (k) breaking POST↔GET parity — the server crontab uses `curl -X GET` at some cadences and `curl -X POST` at others, so both verbs must delegate to the same `handle()` implementation with identical auth + whitelist behaviour. Mocks `@/lib/supabase` (`getSupabaseAdmin` returning a fake `{rpc}` client with per-test overrideable `data`/`error` shapes) so tests exercise the route contract without touching the real Supabase env. All 24 green (`npx vitest run src/app/api/cron/prune-rate-limits/route.test.ts` → 24 passed / 353 ms); `npx tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.json` clean for the new file.

open_questions:
  Q1_safe_templates:
    q: Do we mint SAFE / convertible-note templates ourselves (LawPath-style) or link out to LawPath / CommercialAgreements?
    recommend: link out at Phase 6, mint AU-flavoured SAFE ourselves once P1_dataroom_map surfaces >2 requests
  Q2_wholesale_cert_flow:
    q: Is s708(8) wholesale-investor accountant-certificate collection in scope for the platform, or handled off-platform by the founder's lawyer?
    recommend: off-platform for MVP; expose an evidence slot at Phase 10 that lets founder upload the counter-signed cert; NEVER issue or validate the certificate ourselves (that is a s923B "financial services" boundary)
  Q3_valuation_disclaimer:
    q: Does BlockID's SVI-calibrated valuation output need an AFSL exemption note stronger than the current legal/surfaces.ts:49 wording?
    recommend: add a "general information only, not personal financial product advice per s766B Corps Act" line to any valuation PDF; keep valuation output as tools/analysis, not advice
  Q4_dual_class_capability:
    q: Do we surface Atlassian's dual-class share structure as an option? ASX prohibits dual-class; UK Plc or Delaware C-corp only.
    recommend: at Phase 9/10 add a decision-point doc "single-class default; dual-class needs offshore parent" with links to StartupDaily coverage; do NOT auto-generate offshore incorporation documents
  Q5_secondary_round_workflow:
    q: Atlassian's two pre-IPO rounds were 100% secondary (Accel 2010, T.Rowe 2014). Do we model secondary in Chapter 10?
    recommend: yes — extend Chapter 10 to distinguish primary vs secondary raise; secondary needs cap-table + Right-of-First-Refusal + s708 exemption checks
  Q6_pledge_1pct:
    q: Do we prompt founders to consider Pledge 1% (Atlassian co-founded it in 2006) at Phase 8?
    recommend: soft nudge only; opt-in, never opt-out; deep-link to pledge1percent.org
  Q7_shipit_hackathon:
    q: Do we surface ShipIt as a culture pattern in Chapter 8 (currently only in Atlassian showcase)?
    recommend: add to Chapter 8 sections[] as "Culture rituals — quarterly ShipIt inspiration"
  Q8_r_and_d_tax_incentive:
    q: R&D Tax Incentive is a huge AU-specific cashflow lever. Is it in the guide today?
    recommend: currently only referenced in data-room folder 11 "R&D Tax Incentive Claims" (data-room-templates.ts:1256); ADD a dedicated Chapter 6 section on R&D Tax Incentive eligibility + AusIndustry registration deadline (10 months after FY end)
  Q9_lp_report_bundle_scope:
    q: The lp_report bundling in Chapter 12 assumes reseller = accelerator. Do we support other reseller archetypes (angel syndicate, super fund co-investor)?
    recommend: keep accelerator MVP; extend to angel syndicate in P10+ (needs different anonymisation rules)
  Q10_atlassian_us_facts:
    q: Some Atlassian facts (Rich Wong joining board 2010, ~US$55M cash-on-hand pre-Accel) came from single TechCrunch sources. Do we citation-double-source before shipping copy?
    recommend: yes — every claim used in a founder-facing callout needs a second source; run a citation audit at P4

## 2. Data-room auto-population plan (Deliverable 2)

**Note on count:** The spec said "60-item data room". The actual taxonomy in `web/src/lib/data-room-templates.ts:425-1443` currently has **102 items across 12 folders**. Mapping ≥ 90 of 102 per success_criteria.

**Atlassian registration-statement reference:** **Form F-1**, not Form S-1 — the listing entity was Atlassian Corporation Plc, a UK company, registering as a foreign private issuer. Filed 2015-11-09 ([SEC](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001650372/000104746915008450/a2226437zf-1.htm)); final prospectus filed under Rule 424(b)(4); IPO priced 2015-12-09 at US$21.00 and began trading 2015-12-10. Every "S-1" below should be read as "F-1" — the exhibit-numbering conventions are the same, but a founder using this as a template needs to know an F-1 filer carries different ongoing reporting obligations from a domestic filer (Atlassian only became a domestic filer after the 2022 Delaware redomiciliation). Correction landed 2026-07-31 with `web/src/lib/showcase/atlassian/stage-benchmark.ts`. Exhibit index reachable via [SEC EDGAR CIK 0001650372](https://www.sec.gov/cgi-bin/browse-edgar?action=getcompany&CIK=0001650372&type=S-1). Exhibit numbers below follow the S-1 exhibit-index conventions (3.x = charter/bylaws, 4.x = securities-instruments, 10.x = material-contracts, 21.1 = subsidiaries, 23.1 = auditor consent, 5.1 = legality opinion).

## 3. Next-step nudge engine specification (Deliverable 3)

### 3.1 Purpose
For a given `(user, project)` compute in ≤ 200ms:
- `phase` — the current 12-phase key (1..12) they are in
- `next_action` — the single most important thing to do next
- `missing` — top-5 unfilled data-room categories or missing SVI-criterion evidence
- `readiness_score` — Investor Readiness (0-100) for their current phase
- `nudge_reason` — human-readable "why we are surfacing this"

### 3.2 Data sources (all cited with path:line)
| Source | Table / Module | Fields used |
|---|---|---|
| Phase state | `startup_phase_progress` (`web/supabase/migrations/0049_startup_phase_progress.sql:6-25`) | phase_id, phase_order, status, completion_pct, steps_json, ai_recommendations |
| Account fast-lookup | `svi_accounts.growth_phase_current` + `growth_completion_pct` (`0049_startup_phase_progress.sql:50-52`) | quick default when no per-phase row yet |
| Project fast-lookup | `projects.growth_phase_current` + `growth_completion_pct` (`:54-57`) | multi-project support |
| Latest SVI score | `svi_analyses` (`web/supabase/migrations/0007_svi_analyses.sql`) | latest per project, dimension scores |
| SVI criterion evidence | `evidence_items` (`web/supabase/migrations/0043_missing_tables.sql:59`) | criterion_key, quality_level, file/link count |
| Data-room file coverage | `dataroom_files` (`web/supabase/migrations/0017_user_source_folders.sql:22`) | folder, doc name, present/absent |
| Founder-pack signals | `founder_packs` (see `web/src/lib/idea-phase/persist.ts:213`) | early-Phase-1 hints |
| Fundraise readiness | `fundraise-checklist.ts:319-347` + `computeReadinessScore` (`:350-370`) | reuse the 70/30 blended score, but per-phase (see P5) |
| Existing SVI next-actions | `svi-analysis.ts:250-1400` (`SVIAnalysis.nextActions`) | fallback next_action when phase-specific rule empty |

### 3.3 Output JSON shape (contract-frozen)
```json
{
  "project_id": "uuid",
  "phase": {
    "key": 5,
    "label_en": "PMF / Early Traction",
    "label_vi": "PMF / Traction ban đầu",
    "canonical_stage": "mvp_early_revenue"
  },
  "next_action": {
    "id": "wire-founder-stripe-testmode",
    "title": "Wire your own Stripe in test-mode",
    "detail": "Chapter 5 CTA — a $1 test charge unlocks the Chapter 7 growth wiring later",
    "surface_route": "/dashboard/integrations",
    "estimated_minutes": 20,
    "priority": "P0"
  },
  "missing": [
    { "id": "cohort-retention-pdf", "category": "traction", "phase_first_needed": 5, "raise_blocker": false, "surface_route": "/dashboard/svi" },
    { "id": "founder-agreement", "category": "corporate", "phase_first_needed": 1, "raise_blocker": true, "surface_route": "/dashboard/data-room" },
    { "id": "ip-assignment-founder", "category": "captable", "phase_first_needed": 1, "raise_blocker": true, "surface_route": "/dashboard/data-room" },
    { "id": "abn-registration", "category": "corporate", "phase_first_needed": 1, "raise_blocker": true, "surface_route": "/dashboard/onboarding" },
    { "id": "pmf-signal", "category": "traction", "phase_first_needed": 5, "raise_blocker": false, "surface_route": "/dashboard/svi" }
  ],
  "readiness_score": {
    "current_phase": 5,
    "score": 42,
    "band": "not-ready",
    "delta_vs_last_week": 6,
    "svi_subset_used": ["idea", "market", "customer_size", "revenue"]
  },
  "nudge_reason": "You've completed 3 of the 6 Chapter 5 milestones. Wiring Stripe test-mode now unlocks Chapter 7 in one click instead of a 2-week project.",
  "meta": {
    "computed_at": "2026-07-24T02:00:00Z",
    "fresh_for_seconds": 3600,
    "used_sources": ["startup_phase_progress", "svi_analyses", "dataroom_files", "evidence_items"],
    "afsl_disclaimer": "General information only, not personal financial product advice under s766B Corporations Act 2001 (Cth)."
  }
}
```

### 3.4 API endpoint
- **Route:** `GET /api/nudge/next-steps?project_id={uuid}` (default: caller's most-recent project).
- **Handler location:** `web/src/app/api/nudge/next-steps/route.ts` (new).
- **Auth:** existing `withAuth` wrapper; RLS scoped to caller's `svi_accounts.id`.
- **Cache:** ETag on `updated_at` of the most-recent `startup_phase_progress` row for the project; `Cache-Control: private, max-age=3600` (matches `fresh_for_seconds`).
- **Errors:** `404` when project unknown; `403` when caller lacks project access; `200 { "state": "not-started", ...zero-payload }` when the founder has no SVI row yet (encourages onboarding rather than erroring).

### 3.5 Surfaces (where the payload renders)
| Surface | What it shows | Refresh trigger |
|---|---|---|
| `/dashboard` tile "Your next step" | phase + next_action + readiness score band | on page load + on `startup_phase_progress` mutation |
| In-app banner (dismissible per-day) | next_action.title + priority chip | on every dashboard nav |
| Weekly digest email (see P7) | readiness score + delta + top-3 missing + single next action | cron Monday 07:00 AEST (or founder-configured, per `email_preferences.ts:232`) |
| SVI report PDF appendix | full JSON dump + rendered checklist | on report generation only |
| `/showcase/atlassian` "you are here" overlay (sibling agent's UI) | phase label + canonical-stage badge | on page load only |

### 3.6 Cadence + freshness rules
- **Event-driven recompute** on any of: `startup_phase_progress.status` transition, `svi_analyses` insert, `dataroom_files` insert/delete, `evidence_items` insert. Fire via Supabase `pg_notify('nudge_refresh', project_id::text)`; a lightweight listener enqueues.
- **Nightly recompute cron** at 02:00 AEST covers projects with no events (kept-warm; freshness for the weekly digest).
- **No email spam:** hard rule — never send more than 1 nudge email per project per 7 days regardless of trigger.
- **Kill switch:** env `NUDGE_ENGINE=off` disables the endpoint + cron.

### 3.7 Fair-use guardrails
- **AFSL boundary:** the `next_action.detail` field NEVER prescribes a specific investment, pricing, or legal decision. It only points to a workspace surface. All personal-advice-shaped output routes to the AFSL disclaimer in `meta.afsl_disclaimer`.
- **Wholesale-investor status inference:** the engine NEVER concludes a user is a wholesale/sophisticated investor. That determination is off-platform (Q2).
- **ESIC eligibility:** the engine surfaces a "run the ESIC self-assessment" nudge but does not itself certify eligibility (P6 gate does the check, still marked "information only").

- **P1n** WGEA + Modern Slavery threshold detectors (auto-fire on headcount / revenue crossings) — **shipped 2026-07-24**. Two pure detectors added under `web/src/lib/compliance/`, mirroring the P1i `gst-threshold.ts` shape so downstream cron / dashboard-panel wiring can reuse the same result-envelope contract.
  - `wgea-threshold.ts` — `assessWGEA(input, now)` + `assessWGEAFromHeadcount(headcount, opts)` shortcut for callers that only know a current Australian headcount. Anchors on **Workplace Gender Equality Act 2012 (Cth) s3** (100-employee "relevant employer" definition) and **s3B(2)** (2-reporting-period grace once you drop below 100). Five-branch matrix: `not_required` (< 80) / `approaching_threshold` (80–99 warning band) / `report_required` (peak-in-trailing-12mo ≥ 100 — uses peak, not current, so a mid-year hire spike still fires) / `grace_period` (previously reported but now below 100, remaining periods surfaced in the reasoning string) / `already_reporting` (fires when `last_report_lodged_at` set + still a relevant employer). Also computes `next_report_due_iso` — the WGEA public-report deadline is 31-May immediately after the 1-Apr → 31-Mar reporting period, rolls to next year once today is past 31-May. `WGEA_DISCLAIMER` fixed on every result so the surface can never render the classification without the "confirm with WGEA helpline / registered consultant" hedge (avoids s923B / s911A Corps Act exposure).
  - `modern-slavery-threshold.ts` — `assessModernSlavery(input, now)` + `assessModernSlaveryFromRevenue(revenueAud, opts)` shortcut. Anchors on **Modern Slavery Act 2018 (Cth) s5** (A$100M consolidated-revenue threshold + Australian-entity-or-carrying-on-business-in-Australia scope), **s13** (statement due within 6 months of FY end, governing-body approval + responsible-member signature required), **s16** (7 mandatory reporting criteria), and **s6** (voluntary opt-in for entities below the threshold — surfaced in the approaching_threshold reasoning string as an acquirer-signal opportunity). Six-branch matrix: `not_required` (< 80M or foreign-entity-not-carrying-on-business-in-AU) / `approaching_threshold` (A$80M–99M warning band) / `statement_required` (projected current-period ≥ A$100M — pre-FY-end, warning) / `statement_due_soon` (last-FY ≥ A$100M + FY has ended + within 6-month window, critical) / `statement_overdue` (window has passed, critical + days-overdue count) / `already_lodged` (fires when `last_statement_lodged_at` set + last FY was above threshold). Also computes `statement_due_iso` (FY end + 6 months, clamped to end-of-target-month so 31-Dec-2026 → 30-Jun-2027 not 1-Jul-2027) and `days_until_statement_due` (signed integer, negative when overdue). `MODERN_SLAVERY_DISCLAIMER` cites AASB 10 controlled-entity aggregation so callers know "consolidated revenue" is not just the parent-entity P&L.

Result envelope mirrors the P1i / P1n / P10-s708counter shape: `{matches_atlassian_pattern, overall_signal: "green"|"amber"|"red", cash_pct, rsu_pct, earnout_pct, escrow_pct, splits_align, rsu_structure_ok, escrow_structure_ok, firb_pre_lodgment_required, firb_reason: "threshold_exceeded"|"sensitive_sector"|"foreign_govt_influence"|null, change_of_control_gap, change_of_control_consents_pct, warnings[], recommendations[], disclaimer}`. Exported constants — `CASH_PCT_ATLASSIAN_MIN=0.85`, `CASH_PCT_ATLASSIAN_MAX=0.95`, `RSU_PCT_ATLASSIAN_MIN=0.05`, `RSU_PCT_ATLASSIAN_MAX=0.15`, `ESCROW_PCT_MIN=0.10`, `ESCROW_PCT_MAX=0.15`, `ESCROW_MONTHS_MIN=12`, `ESCROW_MONTHS_MAX=18`, `RSU_CLIFF_MONTHS=12`, `RSU_VEST_MONTHS_MIN=24`, `RSU_VEST_MONTHS_MAX=36`, `CHANGE_OF_CONTROL_CONSENT_TARGET=0.95`, `CHANGE_OF_CONTROL_CONSENT_RED_FLOOR=0.7`, `FIRB_THRESHOLD_2026_AUD=339_000_000` — kept mutable-shape point-values so a downstream UI can render the bands to the founder without hard-coding. Semantics: (a) `normalisePct` accepts either 0-1 or 0-100 inputs (`> 1` divided by 100) and clamps overshoot to 1; garbage / negative / non-finite returns `null` so the classifier can't be fed a lie. (b) `splits_align` requires cash ∈ [0.85, 0.95] AND RSU ∈ [0.05, 0.15]; `rsu_structure_ok` requires 12-month cliff + 24-36-month vest; `escrow_structure_ok` requires 10-15% held 12-18 months — a deal missing all three ranges is `matches_atlassian_pattern=false`. (c) FIRB detection: buyer_is_foreign_govt_influenced=true triggers regardless of value / sector; any of the 19 sensitive-sector keywords (critical infrastructure, energy, telecommunications, port, airport, data centre, cyber, defence, quantum, artificial intelligence, biotech, genomics, space, satellite, critical minerals, rare earth, media) case-insensitively matched against `target_industry_keywords[]` triggers regardless of value; falling below both, headline ≥ A$339M FIRB Register 2026 threshold triggers. `firb_pre_lodgment_required` never downgrades the signal to red — it's a procedural runway, not a deal-killer (matches the Chapter 11 body copy that treats FIRB as a 30-60/60-90 day runway item). (d) Overall signal: `red` when consents < 70% (`CHANGE_OF_CONTROL_CONSENT_RED_FLOOR`) OR cash > 98% (retention handcuff missing) OR cash < 50% (sellers over-exposed to buyer stock risk); `green` when the template matches AND consents on track (or unspecified); else `amber`. (e) Warnings red-first ordered — CoC gap first (60-days-to-signing pointer with the "#1 cause of post-completion price adjustments" anchor), then cash concentration, then splits gap, then RSU structure, then escrow structure, then FIRB with reason-specific runway copy. (f) Recommendations always include CGT event A1 (ITAA 1997 s104-10) timing note + Subdiv 124-M scrip-for-scrip rollover eligibility note + disclosure-schedule mapping to data-room folders 1-8 + "engage specialist M&A lawyer before signing LOI (Corrs / HSF / DLA / Gilbert + Tobin)" pointer; buyer_is_listed=true additionally recommends the Subdiv 83A-C deferred ESS check on the RSU tranche for AU-resident recipients. - **P10-s708counter-adapter** normalise share-register rows into the s708 counter's event shape — **shipped 2026-07-24**. Chips off the read-side of P10-s708counter-wire (still deferred as a whole because the durable share-register schema is owned by a sibling agent) by shipping a pure adapter callers can point at any share-register export today. New module `web/src/lib/compliance/s708-register-adapter.ts` exports `adaptShareRegisterRows(rows) → { events, skipped }` — a stateless normaliser that accepts a loose `ShareRegisterRow[]` (fields optional so callers can feed `equity_events` rows, an ASIC Form 484 CSV, or a founder-uploaded ROM verbatim) and returns a strict `S708OfferEvent[]` the existing `assessS708SmallScale` counter can consume unchanged plus a `skipped[]` audit trail of `(index, S708AdapterSkipReason)` pairs so a UI can surface "we couldn't parse N rows". Semantics: (a) `event_type` classifier maps `issue` / `primary` / `primary_issue` / `grant` / `allotment` → `primary` and `transfer` / `secondary` / `secondary_on_sale` / `on_sale` → `secondary_on_sale` (matches the s708 counter's `S708OfferType` union, which per s707(3) counts secondary transfers within 12 months of original issue against the same s708(1) headroom); blank `event_type` defaults to `primary`; anything else is skipped with `unknown_event_type`. (b) Exemption filter drops rows whose `exemption` tag names a non-s708(1) offer (`s708(8)` wholesale / `s708(10)` professional / `s708(11)` senior manager / `csf` / `s738G` / `prospectus` / `pds` / `ois` / `disclosure`), so a founder who has already classified their offers cannot double-count wholesale into s708(1) headroom by accident. Blank / null / `s708(1)` / `s708_1` / `s708.1` / `small_scale` / `personal_offer` all count — the counter itself is the guard-rail. (c) `investor_id` resolution walks `investor_id` → `investor_email` → normalised `investor_name` (trim + lowercase) so the same person still de-dupes across CSV columns / label conventions and the counter's `Set<investor_id>` continues to match the ASIC "issue" counting convention. (d) `amount_aud` resolution prefers explicit `amount_aud` → `consideration_aud` → `shares × price_per_share_aud`; missing all three skips with `missing_amount`, an explicit negative skips with `negative_amount` so a founder sees the bad row rather than having it silently swallowed. (e) Date normalisation accepts both `YYYY-MM-DD` and full ISO-8601 timestamps (extracting the date part), rejecting garbage with `invalid_date` distinct from `missing_date`. 11 vitest cases in `web/src/lib/compliance/s708-register-adapter.test.ts` across five describe blocks — event_type classification (primary vs secondary vs blank-default vs unknown-skip), exemption filter (non-s708 drops vs blank/null defaults to included), investor_id + amount fallbacks (id/email/name preference; missing-id vs missing-amount vs negative-amount branches; shares×price path), date normalisation (YYYY-MM-DD vs full ISO vs garbage vs missing), and an end-to-end run that feeds the adapter output straight into `assessS708SmallScale` with 19 personal-offer rows totalling A$1.8M plus a s708(8) wholesale row that must NOT eat into headroom — asserts the counter classifies `warn` on both investor-headroom and dollar-headroom guards. All 11 tests green (`npx vitest run src/lib/compliance/s708-register-adapter.test.ts` — 1 file, 11 passed). Typecheck `npx tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.json` green (exit 0). Closes the read-side gap of P10-s708counter-wire so downstream cron / dashboard-panel loaders can pull rows from any source without pre-normalising. Exports: (a) constant `LP_REPORT_K_THRESHOLD=5` explicitly asserted against the reseller-side `K_ANONYMITY_THRESHOLD` so a drift on either side breaks the test; (b) `LP_REPORT_GROWTH_BANDS` — 5-band chip pack (`contracting` / `flat` / `steady` / `strong` / `hyper`) covering the full real line so `pickGrowthBand()` never returns null on a finite MoM average; (c) fixed `LP_REPORT_ANONYMISATION_DISCLAIMER` citing Privacy Act 1988 (Cth) APP 6 (use / disclosure) + s766B Corporations Act 2001 (Cth) so no rendering surface can leak the founder slot without the AFSL + APP boundary on face; (d) `assessLpReportSlot({slot, cohortSize, peersInSameGrowthBand?, k?, revealShape?, cohortId?}) → LpReportSlotAssessment` returning `{ok, redactions[], warnings[], slot, disclaimer}` with a 5-way branch matrix pinned by the test fixture. Semantics: (1) `cohortSize < k` blanks every sensitive field except the low-risk sector + growthPhase chips and reports `cohort_below_k` (matches the guide copy at `web/src/lib/guide/startup-journey.ts:1115` "the shape of your revenue curve is recognisable to peers"), (2) `cohortSize >= k` always strips company name + founder names + customer logos (APP 6 + s18 ACL) and always coarsens exact valuation → 5-band chip (`sub_1m` / `1m_5m` / `5m_25m` / `25m_100m` / `100m_plus`) and exact headcount → 5-band chip (`solo` / `small` / `medium` / `large` / `very_large`) so a founder cannot re-identify by triangulating from the exact numbers even at k+, (3) `revealShape=false` (the safe default) buckets the monthly revenue series into a single growth-band chip via `averageMoMGrowth()` and reports `revenue_curve_shape_hidden` so peers cannot recognise the founder from the curve shape (zero + non-finite entries silently skipped in the MoM computation so a bursty ramp doesn't blow up the average), (4) `revealShape=true` exposes the raw series verbatim only when cohort meets k — the founder has explicitly opted in, (5) `peersInSameGrowthBand < k-1` warns even at cohortSize >= k because the founder is uniquely recognisable inside their (sector, growth-band) slice — the reseller must widen the band or drop the chip; warn (not block) so the founder makes the final call per Chapter 12 mentoring copy. Defensive posture: NaN / negative cohortSize coerces to 0 → cohort_below_k branch; garbage / non-finite valuation + headcount coarsen to null without throwing; malformed cohortId falls back to a generic `cohort-founder-anon` tag. Previously untested — the pure `interview-steps` allow-list + `svi-recompute` snapshot lib + `svi-analysis` signal extractor are all covered elsewhere, but the auth-gated, credit-metered, LLM-backed dispatch wrapper that owns rate-limit + credit pre-flight + `callAI` + `assembled_reports` persist + snapshot-recompute wiring was not. A silent regression here has three high-blast-radius failure modes: (1) dispatching the LLM BEFORE the pre-flight balance check would drain a founder's credits on any 400 (invalid stepKey / no_project), since the app tier has no refund logic; (2) dropping the 42P01 (`assembled_reports` migration not applied) swallow branch would 500 an otherwise-successful analysis on any preview environment; (3) rolling back the credit spend on a Supabase mid-flight race would surface a fake failure to a founder who just paid (route intentionally NOT transactional — see the `// Rare race` comment at route.ts:283). Mocks `@/lib/auth` (`getCurrentUser`), `@/lib/rate-limit/persistent` (`consumeRateLimit`), `@/lib/projects` (`getActiveProject`), `@/lib/credits` (`getBalance`, `spendCredits`, `FEATURE_COSTS.package_agent_analysis`), `@/lib/ai-client` (`callAI`), `@/lib/report-pipeline/agent-prompts` (`buildAgentPrompt`), `@/lib/startup-package/svi-recompute` (`recomputeAndSnapshot`), and `@/lib/supabase` (`getSupabaseAdmin` → multi-table fake covering the four chain shapes the route uses: `.from("startup_package_interview").select().eq().order()` for the concatenated answers fetch; `.from("projects").select().eq().maybeSingle()` for the startup-name lookup; `.from("svi_accounts").select().eq().eq().maybeSingle()` for the FK-anchor lookup; `.from("assembled_reports").insert()` for the report persist). Leaves `svi-analysis` + `interview-steps` + `evaluation-criteria` + `report-pipeline/types` as real imports so the STEP_TO_CRITERION map (idea_and_problem → `idea` + cto lead-agent, target_customers → `market`, revenue_hypothesis → `revenue`, etc.) is asserted end-to-end. Covers: 401 anon short-circuits before rate-limit + `getBalance` + `spendCredits` + `callAI` + `recomputeAndSnapshot` (the strictest gate — anon must never even reach a probe); rate-limit bucket/actor/limit/window pinned to `{bucket:'startup-package.analyze', actorId:user.id, limit:5, windowSeconds:3600}` (5/hour is the LLM-cost-anchored cap at route.ts:76-78); 429 `rate_limited` passes `retry_after_seconds` into body AND `Retry-After` header + does not spend or dispatch; 429 defaults `Retry-After` to `'60'` when bucket reply omits `retry_after_seconds`; 400 `invalid_json` on unparseable body (rate-limit consumed, nothing else); 400 `invalid_step_key` on missing / unknown stepKey — critically never spends or dispatches (proves `isInterviewStepKey` allow-list fires *before* the credit pre-flight); resolves projectId from body when supplied (skips `getActiveProject` fallback) and forwards it into every DB chain — the fake supabase captures `interview_project_id` + `projects_id` so cross-project leaks are pinned per-call; falls back to `getActiveProject(user.id)` when body omits projectId; 400 `no_project` when neither body nor `getActiveProject` yield a projectId (never spends); 402 `insufficient_credits` when `getBalance` returns 0 (< `FEATURE_COSTS.package_agent_analysis = 1`) — response body `{ok:false, reason:'insufficient_credits', credits_needed:1, credits_balance:0, url:'/credits'}` matches the founder-facing top-up nudge shape, and `callAI` + `spendCredits` are both `.not.toHaveBeenCalled()` (the exact regression that would drain a founder's balance on a bill-first, analyse-later refactor); 503 `db_unavailable` when `getSupabaseAdmin()` returns null AFTER the credit pre-flight (never dispatches — the credit gate fires before the DB gate so a broken supabase never burns tokens); 400 `no_answers_yet` when the interview table is empty for this project (never dispatches or spends); 502 `dispatch_failed` when `callAI` throws — carries `detail: <Error.message>` AND critically `spendCredits` is `.not.toHaveBeenCalled()` + `recomputeAndSnapshot` is `.not.toHaveBeenCalled()` (the "implicit refund on failure" contract at route.ts:11 — a founder is never charged for a failed LLM call); `callAI` receives `{system: buildAgentPrompt-result, user, maxTokens}` — tier is hard-coded to `standard` regardless of `body.tier` per route.ts:119 (the `free`/`standard` body field is package-pricing, not report-depth); user prompt contains the startup name (from `projects.name` lookup) + concatenated interview answers verbatim + the `## Startup:`/`## Founder Interview Answers`/`## Current SVI:` headers the agent expects; startupName falls back to `'Untitled startup'` when the projects lookup returns null; `spendCredits` fires ONLY after a successful dispatch — with `{userId, feature:'package_agent_analysis', metadata:{project_id, step_key, lead_agent:'cto', criterion:'idea', display_cost:<number>}}` (the metadata contract billing.metrics + reseller sandbox routing reads at credits.ts:598); `assembled_reports` insert is SKIPPED when `svi_accounts` lookup returns null (FK anchor missing — snapshot still recomputes so the founder's live meter still advances); happy-path `assembled_reports` insert captures the SCORE marker (78 from `<!-- SCORE: 78 -->`), executive summary (SCORE marker stripped from display copy), sections_json (1 entry with id `sec-idea_and_problem` + criterion `idea` + agentRole `cto` + score 78), status `complete`, tier `standard`, locale `en`, credits_cost 1, quality_score 60, title `Package step: idea_and_problem`, account_id from the svi_accounts lookup, user_id + project_id from the request; 42P01 `assembled_reports` insert failure is swallowed — response still 200 + snapshot still runs (no console.error for 42P01 — regression sentinel that keeps the log clean on any preview env where migration 0116 hasn't been applied); non-42P01 insert errors ARE logged but STILL return 200 (best-effort persist — the report is a nice-to-have; the founder-facing snapshot is the load-bearing artefact); happy-path 200 returns `{ok, reportId, sviDelta, svi, executiveSummary, creditsRemaining}` + echoes the snapshot values from `recomputeAndSnapshot` verbatim (svi 71 + delta 4 pinned bit-for-bit); `upgradeSuggestion` field appears when the post-spend balance drops below 3 (the "top up A$5" copy at route.ts:361) and is `undefined` (elided from JSON) when balance is >= 3 — regression sentinel against a founder seeing "top up" on a healthy balance; `spendCredits` race (`ok:false`) still returns 200 — the LLM work is persisted and a `console.warn` "spendCredits race" is logged (rare balance-shifted-mid-flight case at route.ts:283-288 — never flip to `ok:false` on this branch or a paid founder sees a fake failure); svi_accounts lookup is scoped by BOTH email AND project_id (per-project account isolation — a founder with two projects gets two account rows); interview lookup is scoped by project_id; reportId is unique across calls (Date.now + Math.random collision-avoidance — asserted via two back-to-back calls yielding distinct ids); SCORE marker missing → falls back to a mid-range `50` in the persisted section (never throws on an LLM response that omits the marker); SCORE marker of `250` clamps to `100` (route.ts:299 `Math.min(100, Math.max(0, ...))` — a founder never sees a 250/100 score in the UI). All 29 green (`npx vitest run src/app/api/startup-package/analyze/route.test.ts` → 29 passed / 567 ms); `npx tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.json` clean for the new file (repo total error count remains 0). First test coverage for `startup-package/analyze/route.ts` — closes the last-mile HTTP-surface gap on the [[project_startup_package_ship1]] guided-interview stack, completing the P5 route-test slate (write → cap-table → snapshot → dispatch).

happy 200 returns `{ok:true, record:{..., id}, dataroom_file_id, disclaimer}`; 500 `insert_failed` + `Error.message` when the cert insert errors (would previously have returned ok:true with a phantom record); GET anon 401 short-circuits before supabase + getActiveProject; GET 200 `{ok:true, certs:[], summary, disclaimer}` when supabase is unconfigured; GET list query scoped to `compliance_s708_certs` by (user_id, project_id) with null-fallback for solo founders, ordered by `cert_date desc` (UI assumes newest first), selecting the eight audit columns the panel renders; `classifyCert` classifies each returned row into `valid | expiring_soon | expired` (deterministic via `vi.setSystemTime('2026-08-08')`) and `summariseCerts` aggregates the three-status roll-up + `has_valid_or_expiring`; missing `evidence_url` coerces to null (never leaks undefined through JSON). Every one of the six response envelopes (POST 401/400/400/500/200/GET 401/200/200) carries `S708_DISCLAIMER` — the AFSL not-legal-advice wording that MUST accompany every s708 response per `web/src/lib/compliance/s708-wholesale.ts:21`. "deploy-live.sh exit 1". Previously untested — the auth-gated share endpoint that (a) looks up a founder's `svi_analyses` row by `id`, (b) verifies the caller owns it via `email` match, and (c) forwards to `sendSVIShare` with the row's `total_svi`. A silent regression here has three high-blast-radius failure modes: (1) dropping the case-insensitive/trim on the email ownership check would 403 any founder whose Supabase-stored email casing has drifted from the profile they log in with (Google OAuth normalises casing whereas the founder's original signup did not); (2) dispatching `sendSVIShare` BEFORE the ownership check would let a caller enumerate + leak another founder's SVI score to an arbitrary recipient by iterating slug ids; (3) misclassifying `sendSVIShare` `reason:'not_configured'` as a 500 instead of 503 would send a founder into a retry storm against a config-missing preview env instead of surfacing the "wire RESEND_API_KEY" nudge. Mocks `@/lib/auth` (`getCurrentUser`), `@/lib/email` (`sendSVIShare`), and `@/lib/supabase` (`getSupabaseAdmin` → single fake chain `.from("svi_analyses").select("total_svi, email").eq("id", slug).single()`). Covers: 401 anon short-circuits before any body-parse or DB touch (`sendSVIShare` never called); 400 `Invalid JSON body` on unparseable body; 400 when `recipientEmail` missing OR malformed (no `@`); 400 when `slug` missing; 403 `You do not own this SVI analysis` when the row's email is a different address (no send); ownership check normalises BOTH sides — passes when the row email is `"  founder@example.com  "` and the caller is `Founder@Example.com` (trim + case-fold on both sides), forwarding `svi:88` verbatim into `sendSVIShare`; `senderName` defaults to `null` when the caller omits it (not `undefined` — the email template renders `null → "A friend"` rather than the literal string `"undefined"`); when `getSupabaseAdmin()` returns `null` (dev laptop, first-boot, DB unconfigured preview env) the route skips the ownership check entirely and forwards `svi:0` — trades ownership enforcement for uptime on the least-sensitive dev path; when the row is absent (`.single()` returns `{data:null}`) the route does NOT 403 — treats it as "founder just cleared their history" and forwards `svi:0` so the recipient still gets a share email pointing to an empty slug (regression guard against a strict `data ? ownership : 403` that would break the "share your first score" flow); when the row exists but `total_svi` is `null` (analysis mid-computation) the `svi:0` fallback still fires — never sends `svi:null` through to the email template's number formatter; 503 `not_configured` when `sendSVIShare` reports RESEND_API_KEY missing (Retry-After behaviour deferred to the mailer); 500 `send_error` when `sendSVIShare` reports a Resend upstream error. All 13 green (`npx vitest run src/app/api/svi/share/route.test.ts` → 13 passed / 441 ms). First test coverage for `svi/share/route.ts` — closes the last-mile HTTP-surface gap on the founder-to-investor SVI share chain, adjacent to the [[project_startup_package_ship1]] slate.

*Previous tick (**P9-compliance-calendar-route-test** 2026-08-08 — colocated 31-case vitest for `web/src/app/api/compliance/calendar/route.ts`, the GET route that serves the founder-subscribed AU compliance calendar (P1k / P1k-view / P1n-calendar-events) as either RFC 5545 `text/calendar` (for `webcal://` + Google Calendar / iCal / Outlook subscribe) or `application/json` (for the `/compliance/calendar` "Next up" tile + monthly-list founder view). The route composes events from five per-founder tables in parallel (`compliance_gst_status`, `equity_plans`, `compliance_rd_registrations`, `compliance_wgea_status`, `compliance_modern_slavery_status`) — first colocated coverage since ship. Covers: `dynamic === "force-dynamic"` guard so per-user calendars never prerender into the shared shell; GET anonymous → 401 `{ok:false, error:'unauthenticated', disclaimer:CALENDAR_DISCLAIMER}` + short-circuit-before-supabase invariant (auth branch never touches `getSupabaseAdmin` or `getActiveProject`); supabase-unavailable branch → 200 `text/calendar` with well-formed BEGIN/END:VCALENDAR envelope (in-memory render must survive a nulled DB client) + no `getActiveProject` call when DB is unreachable; text/calendar headers (Content-Type exact `text/calendar; charset=utf-8`, Cache-Control exact `private, max-age=300` — never `public`, calendar carries per-founder rows, no Content-Disposition by default so `webcal://` clients don't force a save dialog, `?download=1` adds exact `attachment; filename="compliance-calendar.ics"` header + `CALENDAR_DISCLAIMER` verbatim on the `X-WR-CALDESC` line — regulated-content invariant); `?format=json` branch (envelope keys `{ok, total, next_event, events, subscribe:{webcal,https}, disclaimer}` + `total === events.length` invariant + subscribe.webcal:// prefix + subscribe.https:// mirror + same `private, max-age=300` cache + next_event points at a row in events when non-empty / null when empty — the "Next up" tile empty-state guard); GST gating (BAS quarter events emitted when `registered_for_gst=true`, skipped when `false`, skipped when the row is `null` — pre-onboarded founder); ASIC anniversary (emits `asic_annual_review` from `equity_plans.incorporation_date`, skipped when no equity plan row); WGEA + Modern Slavery fold-in (both `wgea_report` + `modern_slavery_statement` events flow from the latest `result_json` snapshots when `is_relevant_employer` / `is_reporting_entity` fire, both skipped when neither snapshot posted); R&D classifier (`registered` passes through verbatim, any other status collapses onto `not_registered` so a free-text DB drift like `pending_registration` cannot silently fold into `registered`); supabase query shape (every per-founder table filters `.eq(user_id, ...).eq(project_id, ...)` — multi-project isolation; `project_id=null` on every per-founder query when `getActiveProject` returns null — solo-founder pre-project state; equity_plans filters by `user_id` only — no project column; latest-snapshot queries order `computed_at DESC` + limit 1 + call `.maybeSingle()` on all three snapshot tables; equity_plans orders `created_at DESC` + limit 1; `compliance_rd_registrations` does NOT limit + never calls `.maybeSingle()` — every FY needed for buildRDCalendar; `getActiveProject` receives the user id not email). All 31 green (`npx vitest run src/app/api/compliance/calendar/route.test.ts` → 31 passed / 514ms). Zero source-code churn — no route edit, no migration, no schema. Follows the `wgea-threshold/route.test.ts` + `modern-slavery-threshold/route.test.ts` + `esic/route.test.ts` + `gst-threshold/route.test.ts` shape — shoring up direct route coverage on the compliance-calendar path (P1k ship note) so a silent regression in the multi-project isolation, the R&D classifier, the WGEA/MSA snapshot fold-in, or the JSON/ICS content-type + cache-control contract cannot slip past CI. Exports `assessTaxInvoice(input) → TaxInvoiceResult` classifying the invoice into `under_threshold | standard | large` band by A$82.50 + A$1,000 GST-inclusive-total thresholds (per ATO GST tax-invoice guidance under A New Tax System (Goods and Services Tax) Act 1999 (Cth) s 29-70(1)), returning `{ok, band, gst_inclusive_total_aud, computed_gst_component_aud, missing_fields[], warnings[], recommendations[], disclaimer}` with the missing-field union covering the 9 ATO-mandated slots (`gst_inclusive_total`, `supplier_name`, `supplier_abn`, `supplier_abn_invalid`, `issue_date`, `description`, `gst_amount_or_statement`, `document_label`, `recipient_abn_or_name`). Reuses `validateAbnChecksum` from P1g/abn.ts so a typo'd supplier ABN surfaces as `supplier_abn_invalid` distinct from `supplier_abn` missing. Standard-rate GST cross-check: `computed_gst_component_aud = total ÷ 11` (rounded to cents; zero for `supply_is_gst_free` / `supply_is_input_taxed` flagged supplies); declared `gst_amount_aud` outside a A$0.02 tolerance surfaces a warning rather than a missing field so a legitimate rounding edge case doesn't block a founder. Large-band (>= A$1,000) requires `recipient_name` OR `recipient_abn` per ATO; recipient ABN checksum failure downgrades to a warning (not missing) because the field IS present just wrong. GST-free / input-taxed flag mismatch (positive `gst_amount_aud` on a GST-free supply) surfaces as a warning. Fixed `TAX_INVOICE_DISCLAIMER` cites the s 29-70(1) rule + recipient-created tax invoice (s 29-70(3)) + input-taxed + GST-free + second-hand goods carve-outs + "confirm with a registered tax agent" boundary so no rendering surface can leak an OK classification without the ATO-substitute hedge. Input tolerant: non-finite / negative `gst_inclusive_total_aud` coerces to 0 → `gst_inclusive_total` missing field, blank / whitespace strings on name/description/date all fail `nonEmpty` cleanly. Test coverage `web/src/lib/compliance/tax-invoice-checker.test.ts` — 20 vitest cases across 6 describe blocks: (1) `classifyBand` (under-threshold ok+warning, zero-total → missing, A$82.50 boundary lands standard, A$999.99 stays standard while A$1,000 flips large), (2) standard-band mandatory fields (green path all-present with 330÷11=30 computed component + data-room recommendation, missing name/date/description/label surface as a set, blank vs wrong-checksum ABN split, invalid ISO date fails), (3) GST amount vs 'includes GST' statement (both missing → `gst_amount_or_statement`, statement-only sufficient, within-tolerance passes silent, outside-tolerance warns), (4) large-invoice recipient (missing both → `recipient_abn_or_name`, name-only satisfies, wrong-checksum recipient ABN warns), (5) GST-free / input-taxed (both skip the GST amount check + add labelling recommendation + zero computed component; positive GST on GST-free flags mismatch), (6) input tolerance (NaN → 0, negative → 0).
